title: No Pose, No Problem in 4D: Feed-Forward Dynamic Gaussians from Unposed Multi-View Videos
claim: A frozen pretrained backbone feeds specialized trainable heads whose outputs combine into one representation, rendered into consistent results.
layout: 4 columns, left-to-right: input, backbone, stacked heads, results; frozen/trainable icons
description: A wide four-column architecture diagram flowing left to right. The left panel shows multi-view video inputs at timesteps t=1, 2 and N. Each timestep has a central photo of a seated man at a table, surrounded by three tilted camera-frustum icons. The timestep labels are boxed in yellow, green and pink dashed outlines. The second column is the DA3 backbone. It stacks blue frozen modules marked with snowflakes (patch embedding, within-view attention) and orange trainable modules marked with flames (within-view and cross-view attention). Between them are rows of colored token squares and a time-token concatenation symbol. The third column stacks the Gaussian head, the motion head, and the camera and depth heads. Each head has token inputs, DPT or MLP blocks, small renders of Gaussians and motion, and loss labels (L_recon, L_motion, L_distill, L_consis). The right panel shows three rendered reconstruction frames with a downward time arrow. The eye is drawn first to the saturated orange and blue modules and the photos.
caption: Architecture overview. Given C streams of time-synchronized video, DA3 [40] first extracts multi-view features through alternating within-view and cross-view attention layers. Pretrained, frozen depth and camera heads then recover per-frame geometry, which is unprojected into Gaussian means µ. Subsequently, two trainable heads decode the remaining attributes: a Gaussian head predicts static parameters (R, s, α, c), while a bidirectional motion branch processes consecutiveframe features to produce forward and backward linear and angular velocities (v±, ω±), a per-pixel motion gate ρ, and the temporal covariance σg. All outputs are composed into a single 4D Gaussian representation and rendered via differentiable rasterization.
abstract: Recent feed-forward 3D gaussian splatting methods have made dramatic progress on individual aspects of 3D scene reconstruction, but no existing method jointly addresses dynamic content, multi-view input, and unknown camera poses in a single feed-forward pass. Methods that handle dynamics either require accurate camera poses or accept only monocular input; pose-free multi-view methods address only static scenes; and per-scene optimization methods bridge some of these gaps but at minutes-to-hours cost per scene. We introduce NoPo4D, the first feed-forward system that addresses this empty quadrant. Building on a pretrained geometry backbone and recent 4D Gaussian frameworks, NoPo4D introduces a velocity decomposition that splits Gaussian motion into per-pixel image-plane shifts and depth changes, allowing direct supervision from pseudo ground-truth optical flow on the 2D component. This sidesteps both the differentiable rendering that couples prior posed methods to pose accuracy and the 3D motion ground truth that prior pose-free methods require. The system is rounded out by a bidirectional motion encoder for cross-view and cross-frame feature aggregation, and view-dependent opacity that mitigates cross-view and cross-timestep Gaussian misalignments. On four multi-view dynamic benchmarks, NoPo4D consistently outperforms prior feed-forward baselines, and with an optional post-optimization stage surpasses per-scene optimization methods, while running orders of magnitude faster.
